ai.description: *Ichthyophis khumhzi* is a slender caecilian reaching 25 cm. It is dark brown with a distinct, continuous yellow lateral stripe and a yellow-bordered mouth. It possesses 260–270 primary annuli.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Ichthyophis khumhzi* is uniquely distinguished by its distinct, continuous, and broad yellow lateral stripe that extends uninterrupted from the head to the tip of the tail.
ai.habitat: *Ichthyophis khumhzi* inhabits moist, subtropical evergreen forests in Northeast India, typically found in damp soil near streams at altitudes of 300–1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: *Ichthyophis khumhzi* is primarily nocturnal, emerging from its subterranean burrows at night to forage for earthworms and small invertebrates in moist soil.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ichthyophis khumhzi* is oviparous, laying clutches of 25–45 eggs in underground burrows near water. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Ichthyophis khumhzi* is endemic to the state of Manipur in Northeast India, where it inhabits high-elevation regions within the Indo-Burma biodiversity hotspot.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Ichthyophis khumhzi* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, metallic chirps emitted from within its subterranean or riparian burrow habitat.
